summary: Repaired workstation drops BitLocker protector and forces recovery prompt on first post-repair boot
description: Issue summary: Multiple users report that laptops coming back from depot repair present a BitLocker recovery screen on the first boot after reimaging. The machine shows the OS as successfully applied in SCCM, but Disk Management reports the OS volume as 'Healthy (Active, Primary Partition)' while manage-bde reports no protector associated with the OS volume. Impact: Users are blocked from completing post-repair provisioning and require IT intervention to retrieve and reattach recovery keys. Scope: So far observed on two Dell Precision 5560 units and one HP EliteBook repaired during the same repair batch (DEPOT_REPAIR_2231).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Depot replaces NVMe, performs hardware repair, returns device to IT depot
2) Imaging team runs standard corporate image via SCCM/Task Sequence (corporate-image-2026Q1)
3) Machine boots to OOBE, completes AzureAD join and Intune enrollment
4) On first user login the system prompts for BitLocker recovery key instead of unlocking automatically
logs: manage-bde -status output: OS volume: No Key Protectors Found
Event Viewer System: TPM error 809: 'The TPM reported an error while attempting to create a primary key' (2026-03-09 08:21:12)
SCCM Task Sequence logs: SMSTS.log shows 'Apply Operating System' succeeded; no BitLocker step errors
Intune Device Registration: MDMEnrollment logs show device ID match but BitLocker policy applied after enrollment
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 - Initial triage by IT depot: Verified disk hardware and physical connection. NVMe verified healthy using vendor tool.
2026-03-10 - Imaging team re-ran the image on one affected device and reproduced the recovery prompt consistently after AzureAD join.
Hypothesis A: TPM ownership or TPM PCR values changed during repair (firmware wipe) so previously provisioned key protectors aren't valid for the new TPM state.
Hypothesis B: Imaging task sequence ordering applies BitLocker policy via Intune before TPM is initialized/owned, resulting in no protector created (race condition).
Checked AD: DeviceObject has escrowed BitLocker key in AD for the older device ID; keys present but protector IDs don't match manage-bde output.
2026-03-11 - Consulted with Security: Confirmed corporate BitLocker policy requires TPM+PIN for new devices; policy in Intune appears to be applied but local protector not recorded.

2026-03-12 - Reproduction attempt: Modified task sequence to explicitly run 'Initialize-Tpm -AllowClear' and then re-run BitLocker enable step; observed protector creation when run manually after TPM init.

Conclusion so far: Race between Intune/MDM policy enforcement and TPM initialization during post-image OOBE is the most likely root cause. Depot repair that resulted in TPM cleared exposes the timing bug.

Next steps: Update imaging task sequence to ensure TPM is initialized and TPM owner taken before BitLocker policy can be enforced; add telemetry to detect missing protectors post-enrollment and fail task sequence with a clear remediation step.
comments: Maya Thompson (2026-03-10): Filed after two users hit recovery key prompt when returning from depot (ticket DEPOT_REPAIR_2231). Both units had NVMe replaced. Escrowed keys exist in AD but do not match local protector IDs.

Imaging Team - Priya Desai (2026-03-11): Reimaged one unit in lab, reproduced. Task sequence applies Windows Enrollment profile which triggers BitLocker policy from Intune immediately after MDM enrollment. Will try delaying policy enforcement step.

Security - Omar Khalid (2026-03-11): Confirmed corporate policy requires TPM+PIN. If TPM was cleared at repair, PCR values will differ and previously escrowed keys can't automatically unlock. We need to ensure a new protector is created and escrowed during enrollment.

Ethan Rivera (2026-03-12): Performed manual flow: Initialize-Tpm, Clear-Tpm (handled with consent), then enable BitLocker with protectors; successful protector creation and AD escrow observed. Suggest adding explicit TPM init step in imaging.
SRE - Lina Park (2026-03-12): Filed PR to add a TPM init + protector-check step to imaging scripts. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/imaging-scripts/pull/482
Maya Thompson (2026-03-13): Worked with depot to batch hold affected devices. Users notified of workaround to bring device to IT desk for manual protector restore if they hit recovery screen.
Customer note: No external customers impacted; internal devices only.
resolution: Workaround: IT desk can initialize TPM and run helper script to create BitLocker protector and escrow key into AD/Intune. Imaging change in progress: PR 482 adds an explicit TPM initialization and protector verification step; once merged we'll roll out updated task sequence to depot. Pending validation: Run the updated sequence on 5 devices in lab and then deploy to depot. Follow-up action: Add telemetry alert to detect 'No Key Protectors Found' after enrollment and auto-open an INT ticket for remediation.
resolution_status: Partial workaround in place; code change under review
